```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_dplyr <- requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)
options(width = 90)
```

A data pipeline rarely fails loudly. More often it finishes, and the numbers
at the end are a little smaller than they should be. A join quietly dropped
customers whose ids had a trailing space. A conversion turned `"$12.50"` into
`NA`. A filter then removed those `NA` rows without telling anyone.

The usual way to find the step that went wrong is to add `print()` and
`nrow()` calls and run the script again. rewindr instead records the data
after **every** step, compares each step with the one before, and tells you
the first step where the data diverged from what you would expect.

```{r setup}
library(rewindr)
```

## Record a pipeline

`rewind()` takes a pipeline (native `|>` or magrittr `%>%`) and runs it one
stage at a time:

```{r}
tr <- rewind(mtcars |> subset(cyl == 4) |> transform(kpl = mpg * 0.425))
tr
```

Every row of that printout is a state you can go back to:

```{r}
at_step(tr, 2) |> head(3)
step_diff(tr, 3)
```

Code runs in a sandbox environment, so nothing in your workspace changes.
You can also pass a `{ }` block of several statements, and in-place edits
such as `df$x <- ...` become new versions of the object.

## Record a whole script

Most real problems sit in scripts. `rewind_script()` runs a file statement by
statement, splits each pipeline into its stages, and keeps every version of
every data frame. The package ships a small sales pipeline with three bugs
planted in it:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
file.show(rewind_example())
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
cat(readLines(rewind_example())[-(1:2)], sep = "\n")
```

Record it, using `order_id` as the row key so rewindr can tell exactly which
orders disappear:

```{r, eval = has_dplyr}
tr <- rewind_script(rewind_example(), key = "order_id")
tr
```

The markers on the left mean `!` warning, `x` error and `i` information. The
first warning is at step 8, where `as.numeric()` turned some amounts into
`NA`.

## Find out what went wrong

`issues()` lists every problem, with a suggested fix:

```{r, eval = has_dplyr}
iss <- issues(tr)
knitr::kable(iss[, c("step", "type", "message")])
```

`blame()` follows an object back through every step that built it and keeps
the steps that explain its current state. Ask about a whole object:

```{r, eval = has_dplyr}
blame(tr, "clean")
```

or about a single column:

```{r, eval = has_dplyr}
blame(tr, "clean", "amount")
```

The join step carries a full report: how many rows found no match, which
keys differ only in whitespace or case ("near misses"), and which lookup keys
are duplicated:

```{r, eval = has_dplyr}
join_step <- tr$steps[[9]]$join
join_step[c("unmatched_rows", "unmatched_pct", "n_near_miss", "near_miss_keys", "dup_y_examples")]
```

## Get a fix

`suggest_fixes()` turns the issues into code, without any network access:

```{r, eval = has_dplyr}
fx <- suggest_fixes(tr)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(fx))) cat(sprintf("Step %d: %s\n%s\n\n", fx$step[i], fx$problem[i], fx$suggestion[i]))
```

Apply the fixes, record the script again, and compare the two runs:

```{r, eval = has_dplyr}
code <- readLines(rewind_example())
code <- sub("amount = as.numeric(amount)",
            "amount = as.numeric(gsub(\"[^0-9.]\", \"\", amount))", code, fixed = TRUE)
code <- sub("inner_join(customers, by = \"customer_id\")",
            paste("inner_join(customers |> mutate(customer_id = toupper(trimws(customer_id))) |>",
                  "distinct(customer_id, .keep_all = TRUE), by = \"customer_id\")"),
            code, fixed = TRUE)
fixed <- rewind_script(text = code, key = "order_id")
compare_traces(tr, fixed)
nrow(issues(fixed))
```

No issues left, and `clean` now keeps every valid order.

## Scrub through it

In an interactive session, `scrub()` opens the same recording as an app. You
can drag a slider (or use the arrow keys) back and forward through every
state, and see the source line, the data, the diff and the join report for
each one:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
scrub(tr)
```

In RStudio, the **Addins** menu has *Rewind current script* and *Rewind
selection*, which do all of the above for the code in your editor.

## Where next

* The [website](https://neu-data.github.io/rewindr/) has articles on using
  rewindr every day, a tour of the app with screenshots, everything rewindr
  checks, and fixing code with Claude and shipping it in a container.
* `?rewind_rules` explains how to make the checks stricter or looser.
